assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (1985) put electronic structure and nuclear motion into one extended Lagrangian, so that bonds can form and break, liquids and solids can be simulated and finite-temperature chemistry can be treated without a pre-fitted force field. The principle is clear and quantitative, and it opened a whole way of doing chemistry computationally. It is a classic case of a clear physical idea turned into a general capability, and it is easy to explain to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by Car and Parrinello alone, and the credit is unusually clean for a two-person prize. Later refinements (Born-Oppenheimer MD, plane-wave DFT codes) are separate and need not be cited.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of independent use and heavy citation; the method is textbook. Recognition is, if anything, overdue, and the committee would not be at risk of acting on an unstable interpretation.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as condensed-matter/computational physics; Parrinello's later metadynamics and ML-potential work could blur what the citation should cover.
I am relying on memory for the details of the 1985 paper and its priority relative to related work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing changed the scale of molecular biology and medicine by many orders of magnitude in cost and throughput. The chemical core (reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis, and the competing pyrosequencing/semiconductor routes) is real chemistry, with a clear enabling principle: parallel readout of single-molecule or clonal clusters.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa/Illumina chemistry; Rothberg led the 454 and Ion Torrent platforms. Mayer and Ju are credited for related contributions, so the allocation is contestable and requires a decision on which route is the decisive one. A two- or three-person split is plausible but not free of dispute.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of dominant clinical and research use; the impact is beyond doubt, so timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit chemistry-centred sequencing-by-synthesis or the instrument platforms.
Priority disputes among Illumina, 454 and Ju's group; I cannot independently verify the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bifunctional degraders (PROTACs) and molecular glues turn the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome machinery against chosen proteins, using small molecules to induce proximity. It opens a new pharmacological modality, reaching targets that are not druggable by inhibition, which is the kind of 'previously unforeseen opportunity' I look for. The concept is clear and the chemistry (ligand design, ternary-complex cooperativity) is quantitative.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived the PROTAC concept and made the first examples; Ciulli contributed structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex rationale that made the approach general. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue work (Handa, Ito and others) is a separate strand, so the three-person choice leaves out important credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinical-stage degraders are in trials, but approval of a PROTAC drug is not yet established as far as I know. Mechanism is well confirmed in many laboratories; the clinical proof is still maturing, so recognition may be a little early.
uncertainties: Unclear whether the committee would want to treat PROTACs and molecular glues as one discovery.
Absence of an approved PROTAC drug (as far as I know) could argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is one of the most widely used bond-forming reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. The discovery is original and general, with a mechanistic understanding and ligand design that has been refined over decades.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precedent but not the general method. A two-person citation is natural, and the 2010 cross-coupling prize leaves a question of how a committee views a related follow-on.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent adoption; the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: The 2010 prize for Pd cross-coupling may make the committee see this as an incremental extension.
Allocation relative to Kosugi's precedent is a historical judgement I cannot verify here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the delivery chemistry that made siRNA and mRNA medicines practical, including the COVID-19 vaccines. The principle (pH-dependent charge for encapsulation and endosomal release) is clear, and the generative potential for nucleic-acid medicines is large.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group is central to the formulation and ionizable-lipid concept; MacLachlan, Madden and Hope are key colleagues; Langer and Anderson contributed combinatorial lipid discovery. Choosing three from six is difficult, and the credit is spread across academia and industry.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is strong and the impact is very large, but the 2023 Medicine prize (mRNA modification) reduces the clear space for this and the prize may be seen as belonging to medicine.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and the question of whether the chemistry is the decisive element.
Patent and priority disputes among delivery-lipid inventors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a rise in solar-cell efficiency from about 4 percent to over 25 percent in little more than a decade, with defect-tolerant semiconductor physics that is of great interest to me. The discovery combined a materials-chemistry insight with a clear device-level benchmark.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell (2009); Park and Snaith/Grätzel-related groups drove the solid-state devices (2012). Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel also have strong claims, and the field is a priority-contested one with more claimants than the prize can hold.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is validated, but long-term operational stability and commercial deployment are not settled, so the field may be premature for a prize.
uncertainties: Stability and toxicity (lead) remain unresolved, and with them the long-term importance.
The credit allocation is contested and the three-person selection is arbitrary to some degree.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic-code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate non-canonical amino acids site-specifically, which is a conceptually clean way to add new chemistry to proteins and organisms. It is generative, with applications from protein engineering to therapeutics and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal pair in vivo (2001); Chin extended the approach to eukaryotes, quadruplet codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Yokoyama and Mehl contributed related pairs, so the three-name choice leaves out useful contributions.
assessment.maturity: Twenty-five years of use with extensive confirmation, though the practical impact is still more in research tools than in broad applications.
uncertainties: The recent protein-design prizes (2018, 2024) in this area may make the committee reluctant.
Attribution among Schultz, Wang and Chin is disputed in emphasis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis enables radical chemistry under mild conditions with a clear single-electron-transfer principle, and it is now standard in discovery chemistry. Its originality and generality are significant, and the field has had broad industrial use.
assessment.attribution: Credit is split among Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz, MacMillan, König, Melchiorre, Fukuzumi and others; MacMillan is already a laureate (2021), which complicates a fair configuration. I leave out MacMillan here for that reason, but this is itself an arbitrary choice.
assessment.maturity: Mature in terms of adoption, but the 2021 organocatalysis prize and the number of claimants make the attribution unstable.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation and the earlier prize to MacMillan.
I rank this last because the attribution problem is hard to resolve with a defensible three-person citation.
